title: GUARD (fixed in 677af02625) — was: `compset -N` compiled its patterns without `singsub`, so `compset -N '-*' '=*'` matched where zsh runs `=` expansion on the end pattern and aborts with `* not found`

spec.completer:
#compdef fzcs

local -a h
compset -N '-*' '=*' && h+=(hit)
compadd -x "CUR=$CURRENT W=${(j:|:)words} H=$h"
compadd -U -- xa yb

observed.notes: Src/Zle/complete.c do_comp_vars CVT_RANGEPAT runs `singsub(&sa)` before patcompile and, once the begin pattern matched, `singsub(&sb)` for the end pattern. The operand reaching it was tokenized by bin_compset, so `=*` carries an Equals token and is equals-expanded: `* not found`, errflag, the completion function aborts and the line is redrawn without a listing.

observed_when_diverging.recorded_under: main at 87c1835211, target/debug/zshrs zshrs 0.13.56 (sha256 a584f827d2287793), witness completer `compset -N '-*' '=*' && h+=(N2)` under the command name fzp

retired.why: do_comp_vars CVT_RANGEPAT now runs singsub on sa (c:968) and sb (c:982), keeping the operand when singsub raised errflag as C's in-place singsub does (Src/subst.c:521-522).

controls.note: same line, end pattern without a token: no expansion error, both shells restrict words to a=b|c=d and hit
